title: Cameroon Bans Generative Artificial Intelligence in Primary Schools to Protect Foundational Learning
key_facts: Cameroon's Ministry of Basic Education issued a ministerial directive in October 2026 banning generative AI use by kindergarten and primary pupils nationwide.
Named tools include ChatGPT, Meta AI, Google Gemini and Microsoft Copilot.
Minister Laurent Serge Etoundi Ngoa explained the ban on the national network CRTV; concern is damage to early cognitive development and basic reading, writing and mental arithmetic.
Ban covers public, private, religious and international schools.
Teachers keep the right to use generative AI for lesson preparation and curriculum design, but not to give pupils access in class.
Article says enforcement depends on parents managing home internet access and on schools designing assessments that test real understanding.
quote_evidence: The Ministry of Basic Education in Cameroon has enacted a strict nationwide ban on the use of generative artificial intelligence by students in kindergarten and primary schools.
Educators and administrative staff retain the legal right to utilize generative artificial intelligence systems.
why_it_matters_hint: A national government is keeping young children away from AI chatbots in class and at home.
notes: Only one outlet found; no second source. Pool score 6 lowered to 5.
